name: Cummins Inc.
employees: ~67,400 worldwide at 2025-12-31, about 20,000 union-represented under agreements expiring 2026–2030 (FY2025 10-K)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Cummins is the second-largest supplier of data-center standby generation behind Caterpillar, and its Power Systems segment has been rebuilt around that demand — from 16 percent of company sales and 18.4 percent segment margin in FY2024 to 18 percent of sales and 22.7 percent margin in FY2025, with Q1 2026 setting a record 29.5 percent; the constraint is factory capacity rather than demand, with high-horsepower gen-sets sold out into the second half of 2028 and a $450M programme adding 20 GW of capacity to reach 55 GW by 2030. BACKGROUND. Founded 1919 as Cummins Engine Company, renamed Cummins Inc. in 2001, headquartered in Columbus, Indiana, listed NYSE: CMI. Five reportable segments — Engine, Components, Distribution, Power Systems and Accelera. FY2025 revenue $33.7B (−1%), EBITDA $5.4B (16.0% of sales), diluted EPS $20.50 after $458M of electrolyzer charges; Q2 2026 was a record quarter at $9.5B (+9%) with EBITDA of 17.5% and full-year guidance raised twice. Power Systems spans standby and prime gen-sets, engines of 16 litres and larger, alternators (STAMFORD, AvK, MARKON) and, since May 2025, battery energy storage. Per the 2026 Analyst Day, data centers were 26 percent of the segment's $7.5B FY2025 revenue, and company-wide data-center revenue — which spans Power Systems and Distribution together — is targeted at about $5B in 2026 rising to more than $9B by 2030.
ecosystemRole: We assess Cummins as the second pole of the data-center standby duopoly this corpus tracks, and the vendor whose scope reaches furthest down the electrical chain from the engine — gen-set, alternator, paralleling switchgear, digital master control, transfer switch and now battery storage, all under one part-number tree and serviced by a distribution arm that is itself a $12.4B business. Basis: the FY2025 10-K's segment definition, the January 2026 data-center brochure and the PowerCommand switchgear and transfer-switch literature, each of which describes a different layer of the same plant. Collection gap: the corpus can name Caterpillar's hyperscale customers from permit records and campus announcements and cannot name Cummins' — its two disclosed multi-gigawatt data-center commitments, the hyperscaler framework agreement and the record battery order, both leave the counterparty unnamed, so no relationship to a covered hyperscaler, colocation landlord or neocloud can be asserted from any source.

productsAndServices.name: QSK95 Series generator sets — up to 3.5 MW (60 Hz) / 3.75 MVA (50 Hz)
productsAndServices.description: The flagship high-horsepower standby line: a 16-cylinder, 95.3-litre, quad-turbocharged 60-degree V diesel with Cummins Modular Common Rail fuel injection at 2,500 bar, three standard electric starters and an optional fourth, and an optional redundant fuel filter. Per the G9 spec sheet the 60 Hz set is rated 3,500 ekW standby, 3,000 ekW prime and 2,750 ekW base; the G10 at 50 Hz is 3,010 / 2,690 / 2,410 ekW with published fuel consumption of 197.3 g/kWh at full standby load. Cummins builds the engine, the alternator and the controls in-house.
highlights: "100% Load Acceptance in a Single Step" and "Accepts Load in under 10 seconds" per the QSK95 Series brochure — the two claims that decide whether a hall can be caught in one bite
The G-Drive spec sheet states the engine is "capable of meeting ISO 8528-G3 and NFPA 110" and "capable of accepting 100% of rated load in one step"
"25,000 Hours to Major Overhauls" and "20% More Power Density… Highest kilowatt-per-square-foot in its class" per the same brochure
US EPA Tier 2 certification across the G5, G9 and G10 variants — the stationary-emergency class that is cheapest to buy and most restricted in use
Deployed as 18 sets of 3,750 kVA plus a DMC8000 digital master control at Naver's hyperscale campus in Sejong, South Korea, per Cummins' own data-center brochure
productsAndServices.positioning: Sits directly against Caterpillar's C175-20 and C175-16 and Rehlko's KD3250 and KD4000 at the top of the hyperscale node band. Fortune Business Insights estimates Caterpillar at 18 percent and Cummins at 16 percent of the data-center generator market on 2026 data; MarketsandMarkets ranks the 2025 field Caterpillar, Cummins, Rolls-Royce, Rehlko, Mitsubishi without publishing shares.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: The Distribution segment — approximately 600 distributor locations and more than 6,000 dealer locations across 190-plus countries
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Hyperscale and colocation data centers, healthcare, water treatment, telecom, rail and locomotive
productsAndServices.roadmap: Covered by the $450M capacity programme announced at the 2026 Analyst Day, adding 20 GW of high-horsepower output to reach 55 GW by 2030

productsAndServices.name: Centum™ Series generator sets — approximately 600 kW to 3,750 kVA
productsAndServices.description: The current-generation high-horsepower family, described by Cummins as "a new and evolving line designed to deliver a complete spectrum of power." Members include the C1250D6E through C3500D5EB, the Centum S17 at 600–1,000 kW and the Centum Series 78L. The C3300D5EB and C3500D5EB carry what Cummins calls the Centum Transmission Drive, support ISO 8528-G3, meet US EPA Tier 2 with a low-NOx option and carry a three-year warranty. In June 2026 the QSK78 platform — a 78-litre V18 — was introduced to the 50 Hz market at up to 3,500 kVA and 3,300 kVA standby in both Tier 2 and low-NOx configurations.
highlights: The Centum Series 78L is the data-center variant, sold on the Data Center Continuous (DCC)™ rating and paired with a STAMFORD S-Range alternator using 2/3-pitch windings and class H insulation
PowerCommand® 3300 digital control with AmpSentry™ protective relay and NFPA 110 Level 1 compliance
Approved for paraffinic fuels to EN 15940, including hydrotreated vegetable oil
High-ambient and enhanced high-ambient integral radiators offered as catalogue options rather than engineered specials
Gold in the 2025 Consulting-Specifying Engineer Product of the Year for the 1,750–2,000 kW and 2,750–3,000 kW sets; Silver in 2026 for the Centum S17
productsAndServices.positioning: The volume replacement for the older DQ-prefixed catalogue, and the platform on which the DCC rating is now sold
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Distribution segment and the dealer network
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Data centers, healthcare, industrial and commercial standby

productsAndServices.name: Centum™ Force — containerized, stackable gen-sets, 2,000–2,750 kVA
productsAndServices.description: A containerized QSK60-based product in a 40-foot (12.192 m) container, offered at 50 Hz as the C2000D5-PB, C2250D5-PB, C2500D5A-PB and C2750D5B-PB. Cummins describes it as "a containerized generator solution with integrated systems and a modular design" enabling "rapid deployment, space efficiency and reliable power."
highlights: "Stackable design allows for smaller footprint, effortless transportation and lower cost of ownership" — up to 34 percent space-utilisation saving against a traditional build, per Cummins
"Accelerated startup" with an advanced paralleling control module for quick start of multiple units in parallel
Designed to comply with ISO 8528 and CE, manufactured to ISO 9001
Launched May 2025, following a containerized stackable line introduced June 2024
productsAndServices.positioning: Answers the same schedule pressure that drives modular electrical rooms — the plant arrives as freight rather than as a construction package
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Fast-build data centers, rental and bridge deployments, remote sites

productsAndServices.name: HSK78G Series lean-burn natural gas generator sets — 1,600–2,000 kW
productsAndServices.description: A 78-litre V12 lean-burn gas platform, bore 190 mm and stroke 230 mm, sold as the C1600/C1800/C2000 N5CD at 50 Hz on a four-pole direct drive and the N6CD equivalents at 60 Hz through a gearbox. Cummins describes the family as "fully integrated power generation systems… for prime and continuous duty, CHP and peaking applications." Governing is ISO 8528 Part 5 class with isochronous frequency regulation and ±0.25 percent voltage regulation from no load to full load.
highlights: NOx as low as 250 mg/Nm³ (0.5 g/hp-hr), with a 500 mg/Nm³ option — the number that decides what an air permit will allow
Methane number capability as low as 40 on some models, plus low-BTU gas capability
Alternator waveform total harmonic distortion below 5 percent from no load to full linear load and below 3 percent for any single harmonic
Medium-voltage output offered directly at 2400/4160 V through 7970/13800 V at 60 Hz
Step-load acceptance is explicitly not published: the spec sheet states "Single step load pickup: Generator set configuration dependent – consult factory for details"
The C2000 N6CD is one of the two platforms in the Circe Energy behind-the-meter prime-power microgrid in West Texas
productsAndServices.positioning: The prime-power line, and the segment where Cummins is least visible in named awards: trade coverage of the gigawatt-scale behind-the-meter deals names Caterpillar, INNIO/Jenbacher, Wärtsilä and ProEnergy far more often, with Circe Energy as Cummins' one named prime-power campus.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Behind-the-meter data-center microgrids, cogeneration, peaking, industrial prime power

productsAndServices.name: PowerCommand® paralleling systems, switchgear and digital master control
productsAndServices.description: The layer that turns a yard of engines into one plant. Cummins states that "PowerCommand® paralleling systems integrate paralleling controls on generator sets, low or medium voltage power sections, automatic transfer switches and a digital master control (DMC) for supervisory functions," and that "a distributed logic concept is critical for meeting data center redundancy requirements; ensuring generators continue to function under multiple failure response modes." The company says it has "designed, manufactured and tested switchgear and paralleling controls for over 60 years."
highlights: DMC8000 digital master control is described as "completely customizable" and able to "control an unlimited number of gensets, utilities, and loads"
Cummins states the DMC8000 was validated against "more than 1,200 factory tested failure scenarios" — the control sequence, not the engine, being the usual failure mode
Genset-level PowerCommand control provides automatic remote start and stop, frequency and voltage regulation, the AmpSentry™ protective relay and NFPA 110 Level 1 compliance
PowerCommand Cloud™ provides 24/7 remote monitoring across the fleet
productsAndServices.positioning: The seam a single-source buyer is paying to remove: engine governors, switchgear sequence and transfer switch supplied and commissioned by one vendor
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Distribution segment, engineered to the site's sequence of operation
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Multi-megawatt paralleled standby plants, campuses, microgrids

productsAndServices.name: PowerCommand® automatic transfer switches — 40 A to 4,000 A
productsAndServices.description: Six families spanning open, closed, programmed and bypass-isolation transitions. The X-Series covers 40 A to 3,000 A with withstand and closing ratings of 25–42 kA, 200 kA with current-limiting fuses, and three-cycle ratings of 25–150 kA; the B-Series CBL adds bypass isolation from 150 A to 3,000 A. The transfer-switch brochure lists data centers first among mission-critical applications.
highlights: Cummins claims "the highest UL1008 0.05s (three-cycle) time duration and 0.5s (30-cycle) short-time ratings in the industry" for the X-Series

A blow-on high-endurance mechanism "designed to enable the X-Series to carry up to 100% of its rated load after withstanding fault current" — the property that decides whether a transfer switch survives the fault it just passed
Closed-transition families connect both sources "for 100 msec or less", the window that removes the open-transition gap
Thermal cycling qualified −40 to 122 °F and shaker-table seismic tested; Modbus TCP/IP and RTU over RS485
productsAndServices.positioning: One of the seams most often supplied by a third party; Cummins offers it inside the same order as the engines and the switchgear
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Data centers, healthcare, industrial and commercial standby

productsAndServices.name: Battery energy storage systems — 211 kWh to 2,280 kWh catalogue, 5 MWh data-center block
productsAndServices.description: Launched in March 2025 and containerized from June 2025. The catalogue line runs at 211, 422, 633, 1,056, 1,520 and 2,280 kWh in 10-foot and 20-foot high-cube containers on lithium iron phosphate cells at a 0.5C rate, IP55, 380–415 V AC at 50 Hz, glycol liquid cooling and a three-tier fire-safety scheme running from per-cell monitoring through an FK-5-1-12 extinguishing system to a built-in water-spray pipe for external hose connection. The data-center product announced in August 2026 is a separate, larger 5 MWh nominal block with a flexible DC block design compatible with multiple power-conversion and energy-management ecosystems. It sits in the Power Generation business inside Power Systems — not in Accelera.
highlights: The August 2026 award is Cummins' largest battery deployment to date and was written to "utility-defined requirements" for managing AI-driven load fluctuations, mitigating load oscillations and improving ride-through
Data-center block certified or listed to UL 9540A, UL 9540, UL 1973, NFPA 855, NFPA 68, IEEE 1547 and UL 1741 SA/SB
Catalogue units carry IEC 62619, IEC 60536, UL 1973, UL 9540A, UN 38.3 and EU Battery Regulation 2023/1542
Containers integrate the power conversion system and isolation transformers alongside the cells, cooling, fire suppression and site controls
A 5 MW battery system was shown at the May 2026 Analyst Day alongside a large natural-gas platform and a Tier 4-certified diesel line as the three capabilities being added for prime power
productsAndServices.positioning: Puts Cummins in the same architectural conversation as Caterpillar, which pairs gas gen-sets with grid-forming batteries on named campuses, and separates it from Rehlko, which manufactures no battery product.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Distribution segment; the flexible DC block is explicitly designed to work with third-party power conversion and energy management
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Hyperscale data centers managing AI load steps, utility interconnection compliance, microgrids

productsAndServices.name: Alternators — Cummins Generator Technologies (STAMFORD®, AvK®, MARKON®)
productsAndServices.description: The generating end, sold both inside Cummins gen-sets and to third-party packagers, spanning 7.5 to 11,200 kVA. STAMFORD covers the low-voltage range — the PI7H is a 2,500 kVA machine Cummins describes as "specifically designed for standby power, UPS and data centres" — while AvK's DSG and DIG ranges reach medium and high voltage. Reported inside Power Systems as Generator Technologies, about 9 percent of the segment's FY2025 revenue.
highlights: The business traces to 1904; MARKON was acquired in 1987
Alternator choice is what sets voltage dip on a large step, and Cummins sells the same machines to competitors' packagers
Models used across the DCC-rated range include the HC/HCI series, PI734 series, LVSI804R/S, MVSI804S and LVSI824G
productsAndServices.positioning: One of the few merchant alternator franchises at data-center scale, which makes Cummins a supplier to parts of its own competitive set
productsAndServices.soldThrough: OEM-merchant to genset packagers, and captive into Cummins sets
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Genset OEMs and packagers, UPS makers, data centers

productsAndServices.name: Distribution, service and aftermarket
productsAndServices.description: The $12.405B Distribution segment — about 15,000 people across more than 190 countries — is both the channel through which data-center gen-sets are sold and the business that services them for life. Its power-generation sales rose from $3,972M in 2024 to $4,932M in 2025, an increase Cummins attributes principally to North American demand "especially data center and commercial markets." Offerings include the PowerCare® support plan, rental power and a standard two-year warranty, extended to three years on the Centum C3300D5EB and C3500D5EB.
highlights: Distribution power-generation revenue grew $1.0B year on year, all of it in North America
DCC-rated units carry two-year coverage contingent on the set being registered in the warranty system as a data-center application — the rating is a commercial contract as well as a technical one
Cummins' company-wide data-center revenue target spans Power Systems and Distribution together, which is why the ~$5B figure for 2026 exceeds the whole Power Systems segment's FY2025 revenue
productsAndServices.positioning: The asset a competitor cannot replicate quickly, and the reason an equipment sale becomes a twenty-year relationship
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Every installed base Cummins sells into

productsAndServices.name: Accelera™ by Cummins — zero-emissions segment
productsAndServices.description: Battery systems, electric powertrains, fuel cells, electrolyzers and e-axles. FY2025 revenue $460M against a segment EBITDA loss; 2026 guidance is $350–400M of revenue and a $260–290M EBITDA loss. Following a Q4 2025 strategic review Cummins said it "intends to stop new commercial activity in the electrolyzer space" while fulfilling existing commitments, taking FY2025 charges of $458M, or $3.28 per diluted share, of which $415M was non-cash. Amplify Cell Technologies, the cell joint venture with Daimler Truck and PACCAR, targets production from 2027.
highlights: Accelera has no data-center product — the battery energy storage line sits in Power Systems and the August 2026 data-center award was announced by the Power Systems president
The FY2024 comparison carries a separate $312M ($2.14 per diluted share) Accelera reorganization charge
Recorded here because two consecutive years of segment charges are what the EPS line is reacting to, not because it touches this ecosystem
productsAndServices.positioning: A retrenchment in progress; relevant to the dossier as an earnings distortion rather than as a data-center capability

recentDevelopments.headline: James Hopkins promoted to VP, Financial Planning, Capital Management and Investor Relations effective 2026-09-01, reporting to CFO Mark Smith; Nick Arens now reports to Hopkins
recentDevelopments.read: An IR reorganisation in the middle of a capacity-investment cycle usually means the equity story is being managed more tightly, not that anything is wrong.

recentDevelopments.headline: Selected to supply battery energy storage for a large US data-center project — 5 MWh nominal LFP blocks, the largest BESS deployment in company history; customer, location and value undisclosed
recentDevelopments.read: The award was written to utility-defined requirements for load oscillation and ride-through, which places the battery at the interconnection rather than beside the UPS — a grid-compliance product, not a backup one.

recentDevelopments.headline: Q2 2026: record revenue $9.5B (+9%), EBITDA $1.7B (17.5%), net income $932M, diluted EPS $6.73; full-year guidance raised a second time to +10-13% revenue and 18.0-18.5% EBITDA
recentDevelopments.read: Revenue beat and EPS missed on every outlet's basis and the stock fell 7.6 percent — the market is pricing the capacity build, not the quarter.

recentDevelopments.headline: On the Q2 call, CEO Jennifer Rumsey disclosed a multi-year agreement with an unnamed global hyperscaler giving visibility into several gigawatts of future backup-power gen-set demand
recentDevelopments.read: Disclosed on a call rather than in a release, and the counterparty is unnamed — the commitment is real but unverifiable from outside.

recentDevelopments.headline: Phased Model Year 2027 product launch plan announced in response to EPA's proposed changes to 2027 on-highway emissions rules: X15 and X10 limited production January 2027, full production Q4 and Q3 2027; next-generation B platform January 2028
recentDevelopments.read: Rumsey framed it as "about improving the transition, not changing the destination" — an on-highway matter that does not touch the gen-set line but does consume engineering capacity.

recentDevelopments.headline: Quarterly common stock dividend increased
recentDevelopments.read: Capital returns continuing alongside a $1.35-1.45B capex year — the balance sheet is not being stretched by the capacity programme.

recentDevelopments.headline: Centum Series QSK78 introduced to the 50 Hz market — a 78-litre V18 rated up to 3,500 kVA and 3,300 kVA standby, in Tier 2 and low-NOx configurations, for standby and Data Center Continuous duty
recentDevelopments.read: Extends the DCC rating into the 50 Hz world, which is where the European and Asian hyperscale build sits.

recentDevelopments.headline: Circe Energy selected Cummins HSK78 (C2000N6CD) and QSK60 (C1400N6) natural-gas gen-sets for a behind-the-meter prime-power microgrid serving AI and HPC data centers on a 1,950-acre West Texas campus — 10 MW from 2026 ramping to 1.1 GW by 2030 against a 2 GW platform target, deliveries 2026-2030
recentDevelopments.read: Cummins' one named prime-power data-center campus, and the answer to a competitive set that has been announcing gigawatt gas awards for a year.

recentDevelopments.headline: 2026 Analyst Day: $450M investment adding 20 GW of high-horsepower capacity for 55 GW total by 2030, on top of $200M and 9 GW already delivered; 2030 targets raised to 6-9% revenue CAGR and more than 250 bps of EBITDA margin expansion; data-center revenue path of about $5B in 2026 to more than $9B by 2030
recentDevelopments.read: The capacity number is the whole thesis: Cummins is answering a demand it cannot currently serve, and is saying so in capital rather than in price.

recentDevelopments.headline: Analyst Day named three capabilities being added for prime power: emissions-certified aftertreatment, battery storage and hybrid integration, and a large megawatt natural-gas platform; a 5 MW battery system and a Tier 4-certified diesel line were shown
recentDevelopments.read: An explicit acknowledgement that behind-the-meter prime power faces a stricter permitting regime than emergency standby, and that the current Tier 2 catalogue cannot serve it.

recentDevelopments.headline: Indianapolis Regional Distribution Center in Whitestown, Indiana closed permanently, 59 workers laid off between 2026-07-31 and 2026-08-31, consolidating into multi-RDCs
recentDevelopments.read: A distribution-network consolidation, not a manufacturing retrenchment — the capacity story and the footprint story are running in opposite directions on purpose.

recentDevelopments.headline: Q1 2026: revenue $8.398B (+3%), EBITDA $1.290B reported (15.4%) and $1.489B adjusted (17.7%), net income $654M, diluted EPS $4.71; guidance raised to +8-11% revenue; $519M returned to shareholders
recentDevelopments.read: Power Systems posted a record 29.5 percent segment EBITDA margin on 19 percent revenue growth — the single clearest datapoint that data-center demand is repricing the business.

recentDevelopments.headline: $500 offered to owners under Emissions Recall 67A on Ram diesel trucks
recentDevelopments.read: The consumer-facing tail of the 2023 settlement, still running more than two years later.

recentDevelopments.headline: FY2025: revenue $33.7B (-1%), EBITDA $5.4B (16.0%), net income $2.8B, diluted EPS $20.50 after $458M ($3.28 per diluted share) of electrolyzer charges; Distribution and Power Systems both set record full-year sales and profitability
recentDevelopments.read: The headline EPS decline is an Accelera story; the operating businesses that touch this ecosystem had their best year.

recentDevelopments.headline: Following a strategic review, Cummins said it intends to stop new commercial activity in the electrolyzer space while fulfilling existing customer commitments
recentDevelopments.read: A clean exit from the hydrogen production business, and the second consecutive year of Accelera charges distorting reported EPS.

recentDevelopments.headline: Data Center Brochure 5600261_0126 published, stating a presence in 52 countries, more than 33 GW of installed capacity and more than 300 unique data-center customers, with power solutions from 15 kVA to 3750 kVA
recentDevelopments.read: The installed-base claim is the credential Cummins leads with, and it is the closest thing to a market-share statement the company itself makes.

recentDevelopments.headline: Q3 2025: revenue $8.30B against a $7.99B consensus, GAAP diluted EPS $3.86 against $4.87, driven by a $240M electrolyzer charge including $210M of goodwill impairment and a $30M inventory write-down
recentDevelopments.read: The pattern of the year: revenue ahead, GAAP earnings behind, the gap explained by a business being wound down.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess that Cummins' data-center exposure is a capacity problem rather than a demand problem, and that the company is answering it with irreversible capital. Basis: per company filings and the 2026 Analyst Day, $200M and 9 GW of high-horsepower capacity have already been added and a further $450M is committed to add 20 GW for 55 GW total by 2030, with the CFO stating on the Q2 2026 call that the business is "selling out into the second half of 2028" and the 95-litre platform booked into that period. Power Systems revenue grew 19 percent in both Q1 and Q2 2026 while segment EBITDA margin reached a record 29.5 percent. A company that could sell more would not be posting record margins on a sold-out book.

(High confidence) We assess that the reported earnings line understates the operating business, and that this gap is closing. Basis: FY2024 carried $312M ($2.14 per diluted share) of Accelera reorganization charges and FY2025 carried $458M ($3.28 per diluted share) of electrolyzer charges, of which $415M was non-cash. Adjusted FY2025 EPS was $23.78 against GAAP $20.50. The divergence is large enough that outlets quoting GAAP and outlets quoting adjusted figures reached opposite verdicts on the same quarter — a 16 percent miss and a 10 percent beat on Q1 2026. With new electrolyzer activity stopped, the distortion should not repeat at this scale.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that prime power, not standby, is where Cummins' data-center position is most contestable, and that the company knows it. Basis: in the trade coverage of gigawatt-scale behind-the-meter awards, the named winners are Caterpillar, INNIO/Jenbacher with VoltaGrid, Wartsila and ProEnergy; Cummins appears mainly in the capacity-expansion paragraph, with Circe Energy as its single named prime-power campus. The Analyst Day response names exactly the three gaps — emissions-certified aftertreatment, a large megawatt gas platform, and battery and hybrid integration — which is a company describing its own weakness in a slide deck.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the battery line is being positioned as a grid-compliance product rather than a backup product, and that this is the more defensible position. Basis: the August 2026 award is described as meeting "utility-defined requirements" for managing AI-driven load fluctuations, mitigating load oscillations and improving ride-through — duties performed at the interconnection, not behind the UPS. A 5 MWh block with a flexible DC architecture explicitly compatible with third-party power conversion and energy management is a product designed to be specified by a utility engineer and integrated by someone else, which is a different sale from the gen-set.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the Distribution segment, not Power Systems, is the part of Cummins that competitors find hardest to attack. Basis: Distribution is a $12.4B business of roughly 15,000 people in more than 190 countries, its power-generation sales rose from $3,972M to $4,932M in a single year with the whole increase in North America, and the company's own data-center revenue target of about $5B in 2026 spans Power Systems and Distribution together — which is why that figure exceeds the entire Power Systems segment's FY2025 revenue. The equipment is contestable; twenty years of service on the installed base is not.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the 2023 emissions settlement is now a compliance-administration matter rather than a financial one, but that it retains reputational weight in procurement diligence. Basis: the $2.0B charge was taken in Q4 2023 and $1.9B was paid in Q2 2024; the FY2025 10-K records only "immaterial amounts related to stipulated penalties." The residual exposures are the obligation to repair at least 85 percent of affected vehicles within three years and the company's own disclosure that it "has also been in communication with other non-US regulators." A separate securities class action settled for $1.6 million, approximately $0.22 per damaged share — an unusually small recovery that bounds the legal tail.

(Low confidence) We assess that Cummins' exposure to a hyperscaler pullback is concentrated but not measurable from outside. Basis: the multi-gigawatt hyperscaler framework and the record battery order both leave the counterparty unnamed, so the customer concentration behind a book sold into 2028 cannot be tested. Collection gap: Cummins does not break out data-center revenue in its 10-K, no third party publishes it as a share of Power Systems, and the company's own figure is cross-segment. UBS's October 2025 estimate that US data-center generator revenue "could come close to doubling" for roughly $1.5B over three years is the only sized external estimate found.

relationships.scale: Caterpillar 18% / Cummins 16% of the data-center generator market (Fortune Business Insights estimate, 2026 data)
relationships.note: The other pole of the data-center standby duopoly, and the only vendor consistently ranked above Cummins.
relationships.context: MarketsandMarkets ranks the 2025 data-center generator field Caterpillar first, Cummins second, Rolls-Royce third, Rehlko fourth and Mitsubishi fifth, without publishing shares. Fortune Business Insights separately estimates Caterpillar at 18 percent and Cummins at 16 percent on 2026 data; that estimate should be attributed to Fortune Business Insights and not treated as a measured figure, because vendor market-size estimates for nominally the same market range from $433M to $10.34B across firms. Trade coverage puts it qualitatively: Caterpillar "sits first and Cummins a clear second, together accounting for much of the installed base at hyperscale sites." The two are also running parallel capacity races — Caterpillar targeting 65 GW/yr of large-engine output by 2030 against Cummins' 55 GW.

relationships.note: Ranked immediately below Cummins in the data-center generator field, and the vendor most often credited with the shortest lead times at hyperscale nodes.
relationships.context: MarketsandMarkets places Rolls-Royce third for 2025, behind Caterpillar and Cummins, crediting it with traction "in high-density AI and hyperscale environments." A lead-time survey by Terrapin Consulting Group states that "Caterpillar and MTU often have the shortest lead times for larger hyperscale tier units" while "Cummins and Kohler tend to be competitive at the 1,000-2,000 kW range" — a segmentation that puts Rolls-Royce, not Cummins, as Caterpillar's nearest rival at the top of the range. Both are also expanding US capacity concurrently: Cummins with $450M for 20 GW, Rolls-Royce by doubling Series 4000 gen-set output at Mankato, Minnesota.

relationships.note: The fourth-ranked gen-set OEM, competing directly at the 1,000-2,000 kW band and at the top node with the KD3250 and KD4000.
relationships.context: MarketsandMarkets ranks Rehlko fourth in data-center generators for 2025. Terrapin's lead-time survey groups Cummins and Kohler together as "competitive at the 1,000-2,000 kW range," which is where the two most directly overlap. Rehlko's KD3250 at 3,250 kW standby is positioned against the Caterpillar C175 and the Cummins QSK60 at the hyperscale node. Rehlko announced approximately 1.7 GW of hyperscale backup awards in a 60-day window in April 2026, on the same anonymised basis as Cummins' own hyperscaler framework.

relationships.scale: Wartsila: 2 GW of US orders since 2025 against Cummins' 20 GW capacity addition
relationships.note: A reciprocating-engine competitor in the prime-power segment where Cummins is least represented by named awards.
relationships.context: Natural Gas Intelligence's May 2026 survey of the reciprocating-engine capacity race tabulates Cummins adding 20 GW to reach 55 GW by 2030 alongside Wartsila's 2 GW of US orders since 2025, including a 790 MW Texas data-center order in April 2026 and a 412 MW Ohio project. In that same coverage Cummins appears mainly in the capacity paragraph while Wartsila, Caterpillar and INNIO carry the named gigawatt awards — which is the competitive asymmetry the dossier's third key judgment describes.

policyExposure.regime: EPA / CARB / DOJ emissions Settlement Agreements
policyExposure.exposure: Resolves civil claims over the emissions certification and compliance process for engines primarily used in pick-up truck applications in the US. A $2.0B charge was recorded in Q4 2023 covering approximately one million applications, on top of $59M previously announced for MY2013-2018 RAM 2500/3500 recalls; $1.9B of payments were made in Q2 2024. The civil penalty of $1.675B is the largest in Clean Air Act history. Obligations include completing recall requirements, mitigation projects, extended warranties, testing and corporate compliance measures, with stipulated penalties for non-compliance. Per the FY2025 10-K, Cummins has since recorded only immaterial amounts related to stipulated penalties, and states it "has also been in communication with other non-U.S. regulators regarding matters related to the emission systems in our engines."
policyExposure.mitigation: Cummins agreed to corporate compliance measures and enhanced testing under the consent decrees, and offered $500 to owners under Emissions Recall 67A in February 2026.

policyExposure.exposure: Cummins withdrew full-year 2025 guidance entirely on 2025-05-05, with CEO Jennifer Rumsey stating the company was "unable to predict with confidence our expected performance for the year"; guidance was still not reinstated after the Q2 2025 beat. The quantified impact was $22M in Q2 2025. Per the FY2025 10-K, "tariff costs and related recoveries was immaterial for the year ended December 31, 2025" and immaterial to each reportable segment's EBITDA. For 2026 the CFO described the net EBITDA impact as immaterial, with a gross burden of 20-30 basis points of full-year EBITDA offset by mitigation.
policyExposure.mitigation: Pricing and supply-chain mitigation; the 10-K frames the exposure through reliance on "a global supply chain to deliver the raw materials, components, systems and parts."

policyExposure.exposure: The data-center gen-set catalogue is certified across classes: EPA Tier 2 on the QSK95-G5/G9/G10, the Centum C3300D5EB and C3500D5EB (with a low-NOx option) and the QSK78-G12; Tier 4 interim and Tier 4 Final on the DQGAR, DQGAS, DQKAK, DQKAL, DQKAM, DQLG and DQLH built on the QSK50-G8 and QSK60-G16/G17. European and German-market variants carry EU Stage II and TA-Luft 2g/4g. The HSK78G gas platform is offered at NOx of 250 mg/Nm3 (0.5 g/hp-hr) or 500 mg/Nm3 (1.2 g/hp-hr). The certification class, not the hardware, is what determines whether a fleet may run outside a genuine outage.
policyExposure.mitigation: The 2026 Analyst Day names "emissions certified aftertreatment solutions" as one of three capabilities being added specifically to serve prime power, an explicit acknowledgement that the current large-node catalogue is predominantly Tier 2.

policyExposure.exposure: EPA's proposed changes to the 2027 emissions regulations, with implementation flexibilities, prompted a phased Model Year 2027 launch: X15 and X10 in limited production from January 2027 with full production in Q4 2027 and Q3 2027 respectively, and a next-generation B platform from January 2028. Legacy X15, X12, L9 and B6.7 remain available through the transitions. This affects the on-highway HELM platforms, not the high-horsepower gen-set line.
policyExposure.mitigation: Rumsey: "This is about improving the transition, not changing the destination."

policyExposure.exposure: The Centum Series 78L is "approved for use with paraffinic fuels (EN15940), including Hydrotreated Vegetable Oil (HVO)" per the January 2026 data-center brochure. Fuel approval changes a fleet's lifecycle carbon accounting without changing its emissions certification or the pollutants an air permit regulates.

Collection gap rather than an assessed exposure. A full-text search of the FY2025 10-K returns no reference to the Inflation Reduction Act, section 45X, foreign entity of concern, the National Defense Authorization Act, or the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act. Cummins is now shipping lithium iron phosphate battery systems into US data centers and discloses no cell-supply-chain policy exposure. The absence is recorded here because a buyer conducting bankability diligence on the battery line will ask, and the public record does not answer.
